findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, ENOMEM).
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path causes uncontrolled process abort instead of returning a typed I/O error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> (or a domain error type) and propagate with ? or map_err.

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec by index without checking its length. A blank line or a line with no comma yields parts.len() == 1, so parts[0] is safe but parts[1] will panic; more critically the index pattern itself is forbidden by the skill.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed line (empty, whitespace-only, or missing delimiter) causes a panic at runtime instead of returning a parse error.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with proper None/error handling, or use split_once to extract fields deterministically.

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() — unchecked indexing into a Vec built from split(). If the line is empty, parts[0] is a valid empty string, but the pattern is still a Holzman violation.
findings.failure_mode: Same class of malformed-line panic as line 16; also wastes an allocation via clone when get().map(|s| s.to_string()) would suffice.
findings.fix: Use split_once and .map(|(name, _rest)| name.to_string()) to avoid both the index and the Vec allocation.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input, empty second field, or if parts[1] itself panics due to out-of-bounds.
findings.failure_mode: A single non-numeric value in the second column crashes the entire load_sessions call instead of returning a typed parse error for that record.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField)?.parse::<u32>().map_err(ParseError::BadNumber) with the function returning Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>.

findings.problem: .unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy widening-to-narrowing cast. Values > 65535 silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 in the 65536–4294967295 range wraps to an incorrect u16 value, silently corrupting data without any error signal.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside a pure data-parsing function. The functional core must be side-effect-free and deterministic.
findings.failure_mode: The core calculation layer is polluted with I/O, making it untestable without capturing stdout, and produces non-deterministic observable behavior across runs.
findings.fix: Remove the println! from the core parser. If logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer that calls the pure parser, or return a summary struct with a count that the shell layer logs.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() builds an intermediate Vec<String> just to grab two fields. The skill mandates split_once for first-delimiter extraction.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line increases memory pressure and GC pressure (for FFI consumers). Also defeats the bounded-allocation principle since each line allocates a new Vec.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) directly, then parse rest.trim() for the numeric field. No intermediate Vec needed.

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve or bounded allocation handling. The function grows an unbounded Vec from an unbounded file.
findings.failure_mode: A very large input file can cause OOM without a graceful error, violating the bounded-allocation rule. The function contract has no upper bound.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, AllocError> or use a max-records parameter, pre-allocate with try_reserve, and handle the Allocation error case.

findings.problem: No checked arithmetic or capacity computation is used. Line counts or record-size estimates used for pre-allocation must use checked_add/checked_mul.
findings.failure_mode: Integer overflow in capacity estimation could cause try_reserve to panic or allocate too little, leading to OOM on the next push.
findings.fix: Use checked_add and checked_mul for any capacity calculations, propagating errors as Allocation errors.

findings.problem: The function signature returns Vec<Record> directly. Any error from fs::read_to_string, parse, or indexing cannot be represented in the return type, forcing unwrap/panic paths.
findings.failure_mode: The return type encodes an impossible invariant (that no line can ever fail), making the function structurally unsafe.
findings.fix: Change the return type to Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> where RecordError is an enum covering IoError, ParseError, and OutOfRange variants.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation hot spots in the parser path
no allocation audit showing try_reserve usage or capacity analysis
no second-ring evidence (assembly or perf data) for the parsing hot path
no command-evidence gate results (cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test not run in this review pass)
residual_risk: The crate contains multiple BLOCKER-class violations: unwrap on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, split+collect instead of split_once, I/O side effects in the functional core, and no bounded allocation. All unwrap/panic paths must be replaced with typed Result returns before this code can advance. No commands were run; residual risk includes unverified compilation and test status.
